Is Alcohol Addictive?

blocks.html: Yes, alcohol is very addictive. Alcohol addiction it’s something that affects over 6% of American adults. The reason alcohol is so addictive is because of how it changes the reward system in your brain.
blocks.text: Yes, alcohol is very addictive. Alcohol addiction it’s something that affects over 6% of American adults. The reason alcohol is so addictive is because of how it changes the reward system in your brain.

blocks.html: Your reward system is designed to reinforce positive behaviors, things like eating healthy foods, sleeping, socializing, working, having sex, or parenting. The more you do these things, the more hormones like dopamine are produced in your brain. When dopamine is produced, you feel happier; you get a natural high.
blocks.text: Your reward system is designed to reinforce positive behaviors, things like eating healthy foods, sleeping, socializing, working, having sex, or parenting. The more you do these things, the more hormones like dopamine are produced in your brain. When dopamine is produced, you feel happier; you get a natural high.

blocks.html: Unfortunately, with alcohol consumption, your brain releases dopamine when you drink. This means you get the same positive reinforcement that you should only get when you do beneficial activities. Instead, however, you get that positive reinforcement whenever you drink. Then, if you don’t drink, you miss out on that dopamine, and your body registers a deficit, which causes you to crave alcohol again to get that same dopamine hit.

What Therapy is Used for Alcohol Addiction?

blocks.html: There are many therapies used for an alcohol treatment program, and each alcohol rehab near Garland, Texas, will work with you to find a program that includes therapies most likely to help you recover.

Individual

blocks.html: Most importantly is individual therapy. Individual therapy helps you identify things like personal triggers, situations, or circumstances that might cause you to drink. Individual therapy can also help you uncover traumatic events in your past or mental health problems that might make your addiction worse. Understanding these issues can help you develop coping mechanisms or strategic responses to things like triggers.

Group

blocks.html: Then there is group therapy. Group therapy usually consists of a therapeutic setting involving a group, like 12-step programs and AA meetings. Group therapy gives you a chance to identify with other individuals who have struggled and perhaps in similar ways. It helps you recognize that you are not alone and how you are feeling, what thoughts you had, and what failures you overcame. Group therapy is a wonderful chance to learn new techniques for managing stress or anxiety, finding a social network you can turn to for sober activities, and much more.
